_doc: Input-dimension probes for any ship that accepts a pasted text box. Contributed by ship 003 (codeowners rebuild, 2026-08-05). The lesson these encode, learned over six checker verdicts: bounding AGGREGATE input proves nothing, because every DIMENSION inside the aggregate is a separate multiplier on downstream cost. A page that caps 1 MiB and nothing else is unguarded.
assert: Feed each probe into every text input the page exposes. Each must be REFUSED (or answered) within the page's own advertised ceiling, measured dispatch-to-PAINT across two animation frames — not by a JavaScript timer, which stops before the browser draws. A probe that is 'handled' in JS but leaves the tab unresponsive is a FAIL.

dimensions.name: chars
dimensions.why: the only dimension most pages check

dimensions.name: lines
dimensions.why: 1 MiB of newlines is ~1,000,000 lines inside a 1 MiB cap

dimensions.name: line_length
dimensions.why: 1 MiB on ONE line is 1 line inside a 20,000-line cap

dimensions.name: field_length
dimensions.why: THE ONE THAT GETS MISSED. One unbroken whitespace-delimited token inside a short-enough line. Cost 23,701 ms on ship 003 attempt 1, because the token was re-drawn once per matching row.

dimensions.name: output_size
dimensions.why: bounding what is READ says nothing about what is WRITTEN. A view derived from input has no length cap of its own; ship 003 hit V8's maximum string length and threw a RangeError that left the PREVIOUS answer on screen with no error — the worst available failure, a silently wrong result.

dimensions.name: total_segments
dimensions.why: THE ONE THAT GETS MISSED SECOND, and only after the first is fixed. Capping NON-BLANK lines is right for downstream cost and wrong for preprocessing cost: split() allocates one string per line including blanks, before anything metered runs. 1 MiB of newlines is 0 non-blank lines and 1,048,576 segments. Ship 003 rebuild-1 (2026-08-05) fixed a real off-by-one by excluding blank lines from its single cap and thereby opened this hole; the re-checker measured 1,309-1,342 ms reported / 16-34 s wall clock on a fully door-legal input. RULE: the door must bound EVERY quantity any loop between the door and the budget will iterate over, and no raw split may be taken over a quantity the door has not bounded. A page needs BOTH caps, never one.

probes.history: ship 003 attempt 1: 23,701 ms. Rebuild: refused at the door in 0.007 ms.

probes.note: ALSO measure the cost of the PASTE itself: a textarea laying out ~1,000,000 empty lines cost Chromium ~17 s on 2026-08-05 BEFORE any script ran. That cost is the browser's, not the page's, but a user waits for it either way and a page that quietly excludes it from its printed number is misreporting.

probes.history: ship 003 attempt 1 against 5,000 paths: 13.7 s then RangeError, previous answer left on screen.
probes.expect: refused or drawn within the advertised ceiling, with the previous answer never left standing
refused or answered within the ceiling

probes.build: for each limit L: an input of exactly L (must pass) and exactly L+1 (must fail)
probes.expect: off-by-one exact, and the refusal message must contain both the measured size and the limit
an empty state, never a crash and never a stale previous answer

probes.history: ship 003 rebuild-1: 0 non-blank lines, walked through a 20,000-line cap, 1,309-1,342 ms reported. Rebuild-2 (2026-08-06, door.maxSegments): refused in 0.9 ms.
probes.expect: refused, naming a TOTAL-lines limit distinct from the rule/path limit

probes.history: added 2026-08-06 - the previous cap's off-by-one (20,000 rules + a trailing newline rejected as 20,001) is exactly the bug that motivated excluding blanks, so the replacement cap must be off-by-one exact in BOTH directions or the cure repeats the disease.
probes.expect: exactly maxSegments segments ANSWERED; maxSegments+1 REFUSED. Verified at the page 2026-08-06 for 20,000/20,001.

probes.build: drive input events repeatedly (every ~30 ms) while a slow-but-legal input is mid-run, then again at a sweep of delays 5/22/39/56/73/90 ms after dispatch to land inside every phase
probes.history: ship 003 rebuild-1 used `var running=false; if(running) return;` - a lock with no release path on the re-entrant case. An input arriving during the post-paint measurement was DROPPED with no rescheduler, leaving the page on 'working...' with data-state='idle' indefinitely. Replaced 2026-08-06 with a generation counter (gen/painted/busy) where every release of `busy` re-pumps if the newest generation is unpainted.
probes.expect: page returns to data-state='idle' with a real answer; data-state='idle' NEVER coexists with the text 'working...' in the result panel

stale_answer_probe.why: A page that computes synchronously never paints its own clear(), so the LAST PAINTED FRAME during a long run is the PREVIOUS answer — which reads as a current answer to the only observer that matters. Reading the DOM does not catch this; the DOM is already correct.
stale_answer_probe.how: Screenshot mid-run, or expose a state attribute and assert it flips to a non-answer state BEFORE compute begins. Ship 003's rebuild clears, waits two animation frames so the clear is painted, and only then starts work.
stale_answer_probe.expect: no frame during a run shows a stale answer as though it were current

measured_2026_08_05.engine: Chromium 1194, headless, in the build sandbox
measured_2026_08_05.overshoot_cause: drawing the refusal happens after the work meter has already stopped, so dispatch-to-paint is always larger than the deadline; state the measured total, never the deadline alone
measured_2026_08_05.answered_band: 200 rules x 500 paths = 100,000 pairs answered in 435 ms; 500 x 500 = 250,000 pairs refused. Input caps (20,000 rules, 5,000 paths) are READ limits and are far above the WORK limit — say so on the page rather than letting the caps imply a capability.

regression_notes: 2026-08-06: a boolean re-entrancy guard cannot express the question that matters. 'Is something running?' is not 'is the newest input the one on screen?' - the second needs a number. Any ship that debounces recomputation must use a generation counter, not a lock: gen (newest requested), painted (on screen), busy (in flight, or -1). Two checkable properties: every exit from the run releases busy, and every release re-pumps when gen !== painted.
